idiom_name: @discardableResult func withX(...) -> Self on reference types, new-value steps on value types, and library modifier chains (SwiftUI)
implementation_notes: Swift lets a class method return self (annotated @discardableResult so the terminal call reads cleanly), so the classic chain is written directly on reference types; on structs and enums a step either returns a new value or is marked mutating, and because value types are copied the chained expression never aliases the original - the semantics most Swift types prefer. The dominant library realization is SwiftUI's modifier chain (Text("Hi").font(.headline).foregroundStyle(.red)), where each modifier returns a NEW view wrapping its receiver, so a chain builds a type-level tree rather than mutating one object; @resultBuilder covers structured, nested DSLs. What replaces the classic builder structure: memberwise initializers with default values (SE-0242) for plain configuration, and the modifier/result-builder style for anything declarative; keep a self-returning chain for mutable reference types you own and want to configure fluently.
pitfalls: On a reference type a self-returning mutating step looks identical at the call site to a value-returning one, so mixing the two styles in one API makes aliasing (two chains sharing one object) invisible.

Calling a value-returning step as if it mutated (`request.with(method: "POST")` on a let binding) discards the new value; with @discardableResult the compiler does not warn and the configuration is silently lost.

Long SwiftUI modifier chains can exceed the type checker's budget ('unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time'), and a chain whose concrete type changes tears down view identity - split the chain into sub-views or computed properties.
